definitions.explanation: Something done incorrectly; an error in action, judgment, or calculation.
An unintended event, especially something improper or unfortunate.

examples.japanese: それは{間違|まちが}いだ。
{計算|けいさん}の{間違|まちが}いに{気|き}がついた。
examples.english: I noticed a mistake in the calculation.

examples.japanese: {間違|まちが}い{電話|でんわ}がかかってきた。
examples.english: I got a wrong number call.

examples.japanese: {間違|まちが}いなく{届|とど}けます。{心配|しんぱい}しないでください。
examples.english: I will definitely deliver it. Please don't worry.
examples.notes: {間違|まちが}いなく = without mistake, certainly

examples.japanese: {間違|まちが}いがあったら{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: It would be terrible if something went wrong.

examples.japanese: {間違|まちが}いを{起|お}こさないように{注意|ちゅうい}する。
examples.english: I'm being careful not to let any mishaps occur.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{時|とき}に{間違|まちが}いを{犯|おか}してしまった。
examples.english: I made a grave mistake when I was young.

examples.japanese: もし{間違|まちが}いがあっても、すぐに{対応|たいおう}できるように{準備|じゅんび}しておく。
examples.english: I'll prepare so that I can respond quickly even if something goes wrong.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}に{間違|まちが}いがあったら{困|こま}るので、{一人|ひとり}で{出|で}かけさせない。
examples.english: I don't let the child go out alone in case something happens to them.

notes:
COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{間違|まちが}いない (no mistake, certain, for sure)
・{間違|まちが}いなく (definitely, without fail)
・{間違|まちが}いを{犯|おか}す (to make a mistake)
・{間違|まちが}いを{正|ただ}す (to correct a mistake)
・{間違|まちが}い{電話|でんわ} (wrong number)

RELATED VERB:
・{間違|まちが}う (to make a mistake) - intransitive
・{間違|まちが}える (to mistake X for Y) - transitive
